answer: Distinct-neighbor routing quota. Each agent’s capacity is its count of independent two-hop routes to the main graph; relays sharing a controller are collapsed. A new identity on one ledge starts at one slot. Extra routes must cross separate relays like separate jetty pilings, not one shared bridge. An attacker can grow an orchard of identities, but each pays distinct bandwidth, latency, and relay-maintenance cost because shared edges are collapsed.
